svg.aria-label: Payment-rail press for the 16 November 2026 Chase bank outage. A software bug in Chase's on-premise hardware slowed transactions, and the slowness rippled to other banks and Zelle. On the left, the CHASE SOURCE CELL has a jammed gear with a wedge in its teeth, a fallen tooth and a tilted drum leaning on its front face; a feed pipe carries payment tokens to the central TRANSACTION DRUM, turning slowly with tokens stacked on its lid and one spilled on the plate. Five distribution pipes fan out to small bank cells — BofA, Wells Fargo, U.S. Bank, Zelle and other banks — each with a small stalled dial. The PLAID CONNECTOR block has its incident lamp lit and a cable into Zelle. The QUEUE DRUM holds delayed payments beside the lit APPROVE lever: money only moves after a human approves. The status dial's needle sits in the orange outage window. Verified numbers: first Downdetector reports 9:53 AM ET, peak about 4,800 Chase reports around 2 PM ET, resolved about 6:30 PM ET, 5 banks plus Zelle affected, Plaid incident 10:11 AM ET.
svg.text: 9:53 AM first reports · ~4,800 peak ~2 PM · resolved ~6:30 PM · 5 banks + Zelle · Plaid 10:11 AM
